segments.speaker: Sam
segments.text: Sounds like Neil has a case of the green-eyed monster. In other words, jealousy the fear that someone else may take something you think is yours.

segments.speaker: Sam
segments.text: Humans have struggled with jealousy for thousands of years. Jealousy damages friendships, destroys relationships and can even become a motive for murder.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: In this programme, we'll discuss jealousy to find out what happens when the green-eyed monster raises its ugly head.

segments.speaker: Sam
segments.text: Feeling jealous is no fun. Maybe this question will take your mind off it.

segments.speaker: Sam
segments.text: The expression, the green-eyed monster, comes from a speech in one of William Shakespeare's most famous plays.

segments.speaker: Sam
segments.text: but which one? Is it

segments.text: Dr Mielke also notes the difference between two words people often confuse

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: jealousy and a similar term envy wanting what someone else has.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: You could be envious of someone possessions like a new car their achievements like promotion at work or a personal quality like being funny or good looking

segments.speaker: Sam
segments.text: So jealousy involves three people you your loved one and someone else whereas envy involves just two you and the person who has something you want But while these emotions are

segments.speaker: Sam
segments.text: easy to define, they can be very difficult to manage.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Jealousy can lead to controlling behaviour,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: like checking your partner's text messages or monitoring who they see behaviour which

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: damages relationships. But unlike other psychological problems such as anxiety or obsessive-compulsive

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: disorder, many do not feel brave enough to ask for help with their jealousy.
